choices.content: Draw a perpendicular to \(l\) through the center \(O\), and prove that the length of the perpendicular segment equals the radius
Join \(O\) to any point on \(l\), and prove that the resulting segment is perpendicular to \(l\)
Prove that \(l\) passes through the center \(O\)

question.prompt: No common point of line \(l\) and circle \(O\) is known. To prove that \(l\) is tangent to circle \(O\), the usual approach is to

solutions.explanation: When no common point is known, use the approach “draw a perpendicular and prove its length equals the radius”: Draw \(OD\perp l\), then prove \(OD=r\). Thus \(d=r\), so the line is tangent to the circle.
solutions.title: Draw a perpendicular and prove its length
